failure_reason: robots.txt at https://www.nestasia.in/robots.txt (Cloudflare-managed) explicitly names 'User-agent: ClaudeBot' with 'Disallow: /' — a full-site disallow specific to Claude. Per project rule (brief §5), this is a mandatory stop-before-extraction condition, not something to route around. No category, sitemap, or product pages were fetched; only robots.txt was read (a required pre-check, not extraction).
notes: Only action taken was navigating to nestasia.in/robots.txt via the Chrome connector in a dedicated tab (no other page on the site was loaded). robots.txt shows a generic 'User-agent: * / Allow: /' plus a Content-Signal block, but then explicitly disallows ClaudeBot (and Amazonbot, Applebot-Extended, Bytespider, CCBot, CloudflareBrowserRenderingCrawler, Google-Extended, GPTBot, meta-externalagent) with 'Disallow: /'. This is the named-Claude-agent full-site block condition from the brief, so extraction was not attempted and the company is marked blocked rather than guessed at. Tab was closed immediately after the robots.txt check per the tab-hygiene rule. Prior Home-Decor pass (notes/227.md) reached the site via direct HTTP fetch (not Chrome) and is not evidence this browser route is open, since that access method predates today's ClaudeBot disallow rule and is itself now forbidden. If this rule is revisited or the robots.txt changes, Nestasia would need re-extraction — the prior pass's notes indicate the site DOES have a 'Furniture' collection/handle that was excluded from the Home Decor scope, so real furniture rows likely exist and this is not an absence finding.
